hypothesis: Requests254-256 show that coarse post-HOT price-path state weakly predicts WAIT value but does not produce positive economics. Current minute activity plus causal one-second microstructure may contain the missing information needed to distinguish productive pullbacks from continuing decay.

representations.baseline: Request254 first-HOT static + coarse post-HOT path
representations.minute: baseline + current minute body/range/volume/transactions/momentum/activity ratios and deltas from first post-HOT state
representations.rich: minute + causal completed-second features over the previous 60 seconds, including 5/10/15/30-second momentum, activity density, volatility, drawdown/runup, signed volume/transaction imbalance, path efficiency, high/low recency, VWAP location and mean trade-size ratio, plus deltas from the first post-HOT state

targets: fixed entry value at the current pullback state
forbidden: using future seconds in state features
using May11-20 outcomes to select features or candidate thresholds
changing the 2% pullback trigger after seeing results
claiming one-second aggregates are tick trades or NBBO
next_if_pass: Use the frozen rich representation in a recurrent ENTER/WAIT controller under the same 2% structural trigger.
next_if_fail: Current aggregate data do not reveal enough post-HOT state information; revisit candidate/state construction rather than adding more WAIT-target variants.
